description: A module that evaluates a typed formula once per sample per channel, with four input jacks, a knob and a three-way button as its variables

params.text: Sets the variable k in both formulas, -1 to 1
Toggles clamping of the result to -5V and 5V, lit while clamping is on, and on when the module is first added
Sets the variable b to -1 in both formulas
Sets the variable b to 0 in both formulas
Sets the variable b to 1 in both formulas

inputs.text: Feeds the variable x in volts, one value per polyphony channel
Feeds the variable y in volts, one value per polyphony channel
Feeds the variable z in volts, one value per polyphony channel
Feeds the variable w in volts, one value per polyphony channel

outputs.text: The value of the formula in volts, with as many channels as the widest input, and 0V while the formula fails to parse

notes: the module produces 0V until a formula is typed into the large text field; click into that field and type an expression there before patching anything
the large field holds the output formula and the field below it an optional second formula giving the frequency in Hz of an internal sawtooth, whose phase is the variable p, running 0 to 1
the round lamp shines green while the formula parses and blinks red while it does not
a formula may use the variables p, k, b, w, x, y and z, the constants pi and e, arithmetic with + - * / % and ^, the comparisons < > <= >= == and !=, and the logical operators & | and !
the functions available are acos, asin, atan, atan2, cos, cosh, exp, abs, mod, log, log2, log10, pow, sin, sinh, tan, tanh, sqrt, ceil, floor, max and min
a division by zero or another maths error puts 0V on that channel, and the two text fields are typed into rather than clicked, so no help note is reached from them
